steps.title: We build the system

steps.title: It runs — you watch the results

items.q: What exactly does Double O build?
items.a: AI systems that handle the parts of your business that depend on someone replying: answering enquiries across your website and social channels, booking appointments into your calendar, following up with leads, reactivating old contacts, and keeping content going out. We scope which of those you actually need on the first call.

items.q: Do I need to be technical?
items.a: No. We build, connect and run everything. The only thing we need from you is access to the tools you already use and half an hour to walk us through how your business works.

A single system — a chatbot on your site, say — is usually live in two to three weeks. A full build across several channels takes longer, and we'll give you a concrete timeline before you commit to anything.
Yes, natively. Everything we build is bilingual by default — Serbian and English — and it answers in your brand's tone, not in translated-sounding filler.

There's no price list, because a chatbot for a two-person salon and a multi-channel system for a clinic group aren't the same job. We work out what the problem is costing you first, then scope to that. The strategy call is free and you keep the plan either way.

items.q: What happens when the AI can't answer something?
items.a: It hands the conversation to you with the full context, rather than guessing. You set the boundaries for what it should and shouldn't handle on its own.

chatbot.name: Chatbot
chatbot.tagline: Answers every visitor and books the appointment
chatbot.h3: One brain. Every channel. No enquiry left unanswered.
chatbot.body: The same chatbot answers on your website, in Instagram DMs and on WhatsApp or Viber. It knows your services, prices and schedule, handles the questions you answer twenty times a week, books appointments straight into the calendar, and hands you only what needs a human.
chatbot.ideal: clinics, salons, service businesses and agencies — anyone who gets questions before they get customers
points: Website, Instagram and WhatsApp/Viber from one system
Books into your real calendar, not a form
Answers in Serbian and English in your tone

hero.h1: A chatbot that answers every visitor and books the appointment
hero.sub: Most businesses don't lose customers on price. They lose them to a message nobody answered for six hours. This closes that gap on every channel at once.

problem.h2: The enquiries you never knew you lost
problem.body: People ask before they buy — opening hours, prices, whether you have anything on Saturday. If the answer takes hours, most of them have already booked with someone else. The enquiries that hurt most are the ones that never show up in your inbox at all: the visitor who left, the DM that got buried, the message that came in at 11pm.

steps.title: It learns your business
steps.body: Services, prices, policies, opening hours, the questions you're sick of answering — plus the ones you never want it to answer alone.

steps.title: It goes live where people ask
steps.body: Website widget, Instagram DMs, WhatsApp and Viber. Same brain, same answers, same tone everywhere.

steps.title: It books and hands over
steps.body: Straight into your calendar with confirmation. Anything outside its remit comes to you with the full conversation attached.

features: Trained on your actual services, prices and rules
Books appointments into your existing calendar
Serbian and English, switching to the visitor's language
Escalates to a human with full conversation context
Answers instantly at any hour, including weekends
One place to see every conversation across channels
outcomes: Enquiries answered in seconds instead of hours
Fewer repeat questions eating your team's day

faq.q: Will it sound like a robot?
faq.a: It's written in your brand's voice and trained on how you actually talk to customers. Most visitors don't ask whether they're talking to a person — they just get their answer.

faq.q: What if it gets something wrong?
faq.a: You set what it's allowed to handle. Anything outside those boundaries gets handed to you rather than guessed at, and we tune it against real conversations after launch.

faq.q: Can it take bookings for multiple staff or locations?
faq.a: Yes. It reads real availability and books against the right calendar, whichever way your business is structured.

content-dashboard.name: Content Dashboard
content-dashboard.tagline: A brand that never goes quiet
content-dashboard.h3: Your audience sees you every week. Google finds you every day.
content-dashboard.body: Ready-to-post social content — visual, copy and schedule — plus SEO articles for your site. Instead of posting in bursts when someone remembers, you have a queue that stays full and a site that keeps accumulating search traffic.
content-dashboard.ideal: brands that post inconsistently, or have gone quiet altogether
points: A full week of posts, ready to approve
SEO articles that compound over months
Approve on your phone in five minutes

hero.h1: A brand that never goes quiet
hero.sub: Consistency beats brilliance on social. This keeps the queue full whether or not anyone on your team had time this week.

problem.h2: Posting in bursts is worse than not posting
problem.body: Three posts in a week, then nothing for a month. The algorithm forgets you, your audience forgets you, and the effort you did put in gets wasted. Meanwhile the search traffic you could be earning goes to whoever bothered to publish.

steps.title: We learn your voice
steps.body: Your services, your offers, your tone, the things you actually want to be known for.

steps.title: The queue fills itself
steps.body: Posts, captions, visuals and SEO articles produced on a schedule and lined up for approval.

steps.title: You approve, it publishes
steps.body: Five minutes a week on your phone. Anything you reject gets replaced.

features: Weekly social content: visual, copy and schedule
SEO articles written for what people actually search
One dashboard to approve, edit or reject
Serbian and English output
Tuned to your offers and seasonal pushes
Publishes automatically once approved
outcomes: A feed that stays active without anyone chasing it
Search traffic that grows month over month
Content effort that stops depending on free time

faq.q: Will it just be generic AI slop?
faq.a: It's built on your offers, your customers' actual questions and your tone — and you approve everything before it goes out. Anything that reads generic gets rejected and replaced.

faq.q: Do I still need a designer?
faq.a: For campaign work, brand assets and anything bespoke, yes. This covers the recurring weekly output that otherwise doesn't happen at all.

faq.q: How long before SEO articles do anything?
faq.a: Realistically three to six months before search traffic becomes meaningful, which is exactly why it's worth starting now rather than later.

lead-reactivation.name: Lead Reactivation
lead-reactivation.tagline: Revenue from the list you already own
lead-reactivation.h3: You already paid to acquire these people. Bill them twice.
lead-reactivation.body: A voice agent — email and messaging work too — contacts your old and inactive leads with a concrete reason to come back. No new ad spend, no new audience. Just the contacts sitting in your CRM doing nothing.
lead-reactivation.ideal: any business sitting on a database of past or unconverted leads
points: Works your existing database, not cold lists
Voice, email or message — whichever suits
Books the ones who are ready, flags the maybes

hero.h1: Revenue from the list you already own
hero.sub: The cheapest customer you'll ever get is one who already talked to you once. Most businesses never go back and ask.

problem.h2: Your CRM is full of money nobody's collecting
problem.body: Enquiries from eight months ago. People who asked for a price and went quiet. Customers who came twice and stopped. You paid to acquire every one of them. Nobody has the time to call three hundred old contacts — so nobody does.

steps.title: We work out the reason
steps.body: Not "just checking in" — a specific, credible reason to come back now. That's the whole campaign.

steps.title: The agent works the list
steps.body: Calls, emails or messages at a sensible pace, handles the conversation and answers the obvious questions.

steps.title: You get the warm ones
steps.body: Booked appointments land in your calendar. Interested-but-not-yet get flagged for follow-up. The rest are marked closed.

features: Voice agent that handles a real conversation
Email and messaging campaigns as alternatives
Segments by how and when they went cold
Books straight into your calendar
Respects do-not-contact and opt-outs
Reports exactly what the list produced
outcomes: Revenue from contacts you'd written off
Cost per booking far below paid acquisition

faq.a: It is if you have nothing to say. The campaign is built around a specific reason to come back, and anyone who says no is marked and never contacted again.

faq.q: How old can the leads be?
faq.a: We've seen contacts from well over a year back convert. Older lists usually need a stronger reason, which we work out before launching.

Contacting people who previously enquired about your services is generally permissible, but it depends on how they were collected and what they consented to. We go through this with you before anything goes out.

speed-to-lead.name: Speed to Lead
speed-to-lead.tagline: You reach every lead first, every time
speed-to-lead.h3: The first business to respond usually wins. Make that you.
speed-to-lead.body: The moment someone leaves their details — through an ad, a form, a message — the system calls or texts them immediately, while their interest is at its peak and before your competitors have even opened the notification.
speed-to-lead.ideal: businesses running paid ads or collecting inbound form leads
points: Calls or texts, whichever converts better
Qualifies and books before you're involved

hero.h1: You reach every lead first. Every time.
hero.sub: Lead response time is the single most controllable factor in conversion — and almost nobody controls it.

problem.h2: The lead you paid for goes cold in minutes
problem.body: Someone fills in your form at 14:03. Your team sees it at 17:40, calls at 09:15 the next morning, and gets voicemail. By then they've filled in two other forms and spoken to whoever answered fastest. You paid for that click regardless.

steps.title: The trigger fires instantly
steps.body: Ad lead, website form, DM — the moment the details land, the clock starts and the system moves.

steps.title: It reaches out immediately
steps.body: A call or a message within seconds, while they're still on your site and still thinking about it.

steps.title: It qualifies and books
steps.body: Answers the first questions, checks fit, and puts the appointment in your calendar. You get a warm, briefed lead.

features: Fires on ad leads, forms and inbound messages
Voice call or SMS/WhatsApp, or both in sequence
Qualifies against your criteria before booking
Retries on a schedule if there's no answer
Hands off to a human whenever you want it to
Logs everything back to your CRM
outcomes: Higher conversion from the same ad spend
Leads reached before competitors see them
No more leads dying in an unwatched inbox

faq.q: Won't an instant call feel pushy?
faq.a: It reads as attentive, not pushy — they submitted the form seconds ago and are still thinking about it. Response rates are dramatically higher than the next-morning call.

faq.q: What if I'd rather my own team called?
faq.a: Then the system texts first to hold their attention and alerts your team immediately, so the human call happens while it still counts.

faq.q: Does it work with my ad platform?
faq.a: Meta and Google lead forms, website forms and most CRMs, yes. We confirm your specific stack on the call.

ai-ugc-creatives.name: AI UGC Creatives
ai-ugc-creatives.tagline: More creatives, faster testing, a fraction of the cost
ai-ugc-creatives.h3: Thirty ad variants a month instead of three.
ai-ugc-creatives.body: AI-generated UGC-style video ads — no creator hunting, no shoot scheduling, no waiting two weeks for a revision. More variants means more tests, faster learning and a lower cost per winning ad.
ai-ugc-creatives.ideal: e-commerce and DTC brands that live or die on UGC ad performance
points: Batches of variants, not one hero video
New hooks tested weekly, not quarterly
No creator sourcing or shoot logistics

hero.h1: More creatives, faster testing, a fraction of the cost
hero.sub: Creative volume is the lever on paid social. Most brands can't pull it because every video costs a creator, a brief and two weeks.

problem.h2: Three creatives a month can't find a winner
problem.body: Paid social rewards volume: the more hooks you test, the faster you find the one that works. But sourcing creators, briefing, shooting and revising caps most brands at a handful of assets a month — so you're optimising budget around creative you already know is mediocre.

steps.title: We build the hook bank
steps.body: Angles, objections and openers pulled from your reviews, your ads data and your customers' actual language.

steps.title: Variants get produced in batches
steps.body: Multiple presenters, hooks and edits per concept, formatted for each placement.

steps.title: You test and we iterate
steps.body: Winners get more variants built around them. Losers get cut. The bank keeps growing.

features: UGC-style video ads without creators
Batches of hook and angle variants
Formatted for Reels, TikTok and Shorts
Serbian and English voiceover
Iterated against your actual ad performance
Turnaround in days, not weeks
outcomes: More tests per month at a lower cost per asset
Creative that stops being the bottleneck

faq.a: Some will. In practice what matters on paid social is whether the hook stops the scroll — and you can test far more hooks this way than with live creators.

faq.q: Can it replace real UGC entirely?
faq.a: We wouldn't recommend it. Use this for volume and testing, then put budget behind real creators for the angles that prove out.

faq.q: Do I need existing ad data?
faq.a: It helps, but it isn't required. Without it we build the first hook bank from reviews, objections and competitor angles.

ai-receptionist.name: AI Receptionist
ai-receptionist.h3: Once the chatbot covers messages, the phone is the last gap.
ai-receptionist.body: An AI receptionist answers incoming calls in your brand's voice, handles the routine questions and books appointments. It's the natural upgrade once written enquiries are covered and missed calls are the thing still costing you.
ai-receptionist.ideal: businesses where plenty of phone calls remain even after the chatbot
points: Answers on the first ring, always
Transfers to a human when it should

hero.sub: A missed call is rarely a callback. Usually it's a customer who dialled the next number on the list.

problem.h2: Nobody leaves a voicemail any more
problem.body: You're with a customer, it's after hours, or everyone's on another line. The phone rings out. That caller doesn't wait — they ring the next business that comes up. You never find out it happened.

steps.title: It picks up what you can't
steps.body: After hours, during the rush, or when every line is busy — whichever rules you set.

steps.title: It handles the routine
steps.body: Opening hours, prices, availability, directions — the calls that don't need you specifically.

steps.title: It books or transfers
steps.body: Appointment straight into the calendar, or a warm transfer to a human with context when it matters.

features: Natural voice in Serbian or English
Answers immediately, 24/7 or on your schedule
Books into your existing calendar
Transfers to a human on your rules
Sends you a summary of every call
Works alongside the chatbot on one knowledge base
outcomes: No more calls ringing out unanswered
Your team interrupted only when it matters

faq.q: Should I start with this or the chatbot?
faq.a: Almost always the chatbot. It's cheaper, covers more enquiries and proves the knowledge base. The receptionist makes sense once written enquiries are handled and missed calls are what's left.
Many can, and that's fine — the alternative was nobody answering. It says what it is if asked, and transfers to a human whenever the caller wants one.
It covers the calls that currently go unanswered and the routine questions that eat their day. Most clients use it to make a human receptionist more effective, not to remove one.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what Double O collects when you use this website, why, and what your rights are. If anything here is unclear, email us and we'll answer plainly.

sections.b: Two things. If you send us a message — through the contact form, the chatbot, or email — we receive what you wrote and any contact details you included. Separately, we collect anonymous usage analytics: which pages were viewed, roughly where in the world from, and what kind of device. That analytics data is not tied to your identity.

Conversations with the chatbot on this site are processed to generate a reply and are stored so the conversation has context. Please don't send sensitive personal information through it — for anything of that nature, email us directly.

To answer your enquiry, to arrange a call if you ask for one, and to understand which parts of the site are useful. We do not sell your data, and we do not share it with third parties for their own marketing.

Enquiries are kept for as long as we have an active or prospective working relationship, then deleted. Chatbot conversations are retained for a limited period for quality and debugging. Analytics data is aggregated and anonymous.
You can ask us what we hold about you, ask for it to be corrected, or ask for it to be deleted. Email us and we'll action it — there's no form to fill in.
Questions about any of this go to lazar.gosic@doubleo.agency.
